title: Naked Fossil Fuel Corruption
author: Basav Sen
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/IMG_2248-680x490.jpeg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/07/24/naked-
fossil-fuel-corruption/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/07/IMG_2248-680x490.jpeg)

John Amos coal-fired power plant, Winfield, West Virginia. Photo: Jeffrey St.
Clair.

The 2026 heatwave is a global phenomenon, inflicting extreme temperatures on
billions of people from the United States to
[Europe](https://weather.com/2026/06/23/news/brutal-heat-wave-grips-europe)
and [South Asia](https://theconversation.com/too-hot-too-humid-why-the-
sustained-heatwave-in-india-and-pakistan-is-so-dangerous-283762).

[Extreme heat is deadly.](https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-
sheets/detail/climate-change-heat-and-health) In Europe, an estimated [10,000
people have died](https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/europe-
recorded-10000-excess-deaths-during-late-june-heatwave-data-show-2026-07-12/)
from heat this summer, and the official count of a [few dozen
deaths](https://theconversation.com/too-hot-too-humid-why-the-sustained-
heatwave-in-india-and-pakistan-is-so-dangerous-283762) in India and Pakistan
is [likely to be too low by several orders of
magnitude](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/environmental-
health/articles/10.3389/fenvh.2026.1789071/full), according to a recent
scientific study.

Dozens of Americans died from heat [over the Fourth of July weekend
alone](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/05/heatwave-deaths-
weather) — a toll that’s still unacceptably high.

Meanwhile, much of the country has been [blanketed in smoke from wildfires in
Canada and Minnesota](https://yaleclimateconnections.org/2026/07/dangerous-
and-historic-wildfire-smoke-pollution-event-engulfs-the-u-s-and-canada/),
triggered by the hot and dry conditions arising from the heatwaves. Like heat,
wildfire smoke is also deadly. A similar wildfire smoke event in 2023 led to
an estimated [33,000 premature
deaths](https://yaleclimateconnections.org/2026/07/dangerous-and-historic-
wildfire-smoke-pollution-event-engulfs-the-u-s-and-canada/) in the U.S. alone.

Scientists have found that all of these [regional
heatwaves](https://www.worldweatherattribution.org/fossil-fuel-emissions-have-
rapidly-worsened-european-heatwaves-in-just-a-few-decades/) were made
[likelier](https://www.worldweatherattribution.org/climate-change-exposes-
hundreds-of-millions-to-longer-and-deadlier-pre-monsoon-heat-in-south-asia/)
and [more severe](https://www.worldweatherattribution.org/fossil-fuels-are-
heating-americas-250th-birthday/) because of human-caused climate change,
mainly attributable to burning fossil fuels.

[Major oil and gas
corporations](https://insideclimatenews.org/news/16092015/exxons-own-research-
confirmed-fossil-fuels-role-in-global-warming/) have [known for
decades](https://insideclimatenews.org/news/22122015/exxon-mobil-oil-industry-
peers-knew-about-climate-change-dangers-1970s-american-petroleum-institute-
api-shell-chevron-texaco/) that their business model would cause disasters
like these. Their response was to [minimize or even hide their
findings](https://insideclimatenews.org/news/22102015/exxon-sowed-doubt-about-
climate-science-for-decades-by-stressing-uncertainty/) to keep the public in
the dark about the risks — and [pay front
groups](https://www.ucs.org/sites/default/files/2025-05/Decades-of-Deceit-
report-f.pdf) to deceive them.

This drive to preserve profits at the expense of humanity has understandably
caused outrage. Eleven U.S. states, two tribes, and dozens of local
governments are [suing fossil fuel corporations for
damages](https://climateintegrity.org/lawsuits) for the harm they’ve suffered
from climate disasters.

[State legislators have also joined the
fray](https://www.pillsburylaw.com/en/news-and-insights/climate-superfund-
map.html). New York and Vermont have passed “[Climate
Superfund](https://blogs.law.columbia.edu/climatechange/2024/03/14/state-
climate-superfund-bills-what-you-need-to-know/)” bills that require fossil
fuel corporations to pay for economic losses arising from extreme heat,
wildfires, droughts, hurricanes, and flooding. Similar laws are being
considered in [Massachusetts](https://malegislature.gov/Bills/194/H1014), [New
Jersey](https://www.njleg.state.nj.us/bill-search/2026/S2338/bill-text), and
[Rhode Island](https://actionnetwork.org/petitions/ri-mpp-26).

The U.S. has experienced [more than $200 billion in climate damages every
year](https://www.climatecentral.org/climate-services/billion-dollar-
disasters/time-series) since 2016, and it’s only fair that fossil fuel
corporations pay for some of the damage caused by their reckless greed.

But instead of trying to make Big Oil pay up, some lawmakers in Congress are
trying to do the opposite. Rep. Harriet Hageman (R-WY) and Sen. Ted Cruz
(R-TX) have introduced [House](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-
congress/house-bill/8330/cosponsors?s=1&r=1) and
[Senate](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-
bill/4340?s=1&r=1) bills, respectively, that seek to dismiss [ongoing climate
damages lawsuits](https://climateintegrity.org/lawsuits), shield Big Oil from
similar future cases, pre-empt state Climate Superfund laws, and — most
outrageously — block _any_ state level regulation of greenhouse gases.

This is legislation expressly designed to protect a powerful, wealthy industry
from having to face any accountability for harming the public. And when you
follow the money, you can see why.

Rep. Hageman has received [more than
$23,000](https://www.opensecrets.org/profiles/harriet-
hageman/us_congress/industries?mpid=1088220) in campaign money from the
petroleum refining and marketing industry in this cycle, making it the second
biggest industry (after sugar) backing her candidacy. She’s also received
thousands more from other fossil fuel interests.

Also in this cycle alone, Sen. Cruz has gotten [more than
$129,000](https://www.opensecrets.org/profiles/ted-
cruz/us_congress/industries?mpid=1148731) in contributions from different
segments of the oil and gas industry.

Effectively, these legislators — like too many others — were bought by a
powerful industry to put their corporate interests over the health, and the
very lives, of the broader public. This is naked corruption.

And if we want the kind of democracy we need and deserve, the rest of us
shouldn’t tolerate it anymore.
